record.title: Three Pagodas closure during DKBA–Thai road-maintenance dispute
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.movement: Primarily large cargo vehicles, with changing restrictions on pedestrians, workers, school buses and smaller vehicles.
record.exceptions: June 20: individuals carrying small goods could cross. July 2: workers/school buses allowed at specified hours and paid small-truck passage reported. August 18: pedestrian-only easing, vehicles still excluded in KIC account.
record.imposing_authority: DKBA / Myanmar-side and Thai border authorities
record.enforcement: Resident confirms renewed pedestrian passage but no vehicles.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; current status not inferred.
record.official_rationale: No formal official explanation retrieved; KIC attributes closure to a road-maintenance dispute.
record.context: Worker protests and bilateral discussions preceded reopening.
record.uncertainty: June 17 onset independently corroborated, but initial prohibition mainly cargo. IMNA June/July describes continuing pedestrian and some vehicle passage, whereas KIC August reports pedestrian reopening. Treat as changing restriction regime; no 62-day continuous all-traffic interval. Official state media denied broad closure reports; exact gate/category mapping still imperfect.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. August 18 is a later pedestrian easing phase, not first passage after June 17.

This classification does not make DKBA a recognised state. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): KIC attributes the closure to a DKBA-Thai border-authority dispute over road maintenance; the actor description does not imply recognition as a state. Other rationale codes retain their existing evidence qualifications.
Large trucks barred, while small paid passages, workers and school buses remained possible in July.
Changing category coverage prevents an uninterrupted all-traffic interval.
